title: Spider-Man: Brand New Day Closes Historic India Run With Rs. 504 Crore Haul
excerpt: Tom Holland's Marvel epic wrapped its nine-week theatrical run with ₹504 crore net in India, becoming the year's second-highest-grossing release and setting a new benchmark for Hollywood films in the country.
body:
• Spider-Man: Brand New Day has wrapped its Indian theatrical run with an estimated ₹504 crore net, crossing the ₹500 crore milestone that eludes most Hollywood releases in the country.
  • Multiple trade trackers — Koimoi (₹503.43 crore), Bollywood Hungama (₹503.73 crore) — converge on a closing total, making it the second-highest-grossing film of 2026 in India.
  • Directed by Destin Daniel Cretton and starring Tom Holland, the film opened at ₹61 crore and multiplied its first-day take more than eightfold over a nine-week run.
  • The run cements Hollywood tentpoles as legitimate challengers to Bollywood blockbusters at the Indian box office.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day has ended its theatrical run in India with an estimated ₹504 crore in net collections, closing the chapter on one of the most lucrative Hollywood runs the Indian box office has ever seen. After nine weeks in theatres, the film now stands as the second-highest-grossing release of 2026 in India — a milestone that redefines what a Western import can achieve in the world's largest moviegoing market.

A Nine-Week Run That Defied Gravity

The Tom Holland-led film, directed by Destin Daniel Cretton, opened in India on July 31 with a flying ₹61 crore opening day. Trade analysts expected a fast burn — massive openings followed by steep drops are typical for franchise films — but Brand New Day held. It collected roughly ₹336 crore in its extended first week, added ₹111.78 crore in week two, and crossed the ₹500 crore mark by weekend six, before its run finally tapered off as new releases like Drishyam 3 arrived.

That eightfold-plus multiple of the opening day is the statistic trade watchers keep returning to. Opening-day multipliers of this magnitude usually belong to star-driven Hindi films with deep fan bases, not imported superhero fare. Koimoi, which has tracked the film through its entire run, pegs the final India net at ₹503.43 crore (₹594.07 crore gross), while Bollywood Hungama's tracker puts it at ₹503.73 crore. The two figures are within a rounding error of each other — rare agreement in the often-disputed world of box office reporting.

Why It's Historic

The ₹500 crore net club in India has long been the exclusive domain of Hindi blockbusters. Hollywood films have cracked it before, but never with this kind of breathing room. Brand New Day finished ahead of Border 2 (₹341.70 crore) — the year's biggest homegrown war epic — and left big Hindi titles like The Odyssey (₹178.16 crore) and Bhoot Bangla (₹168.26 crore) far behind. Only Dhurandhar: The Revenge, at ₹1,108.09 crore, stands above it on the 2026 chart.

By Koimoi's valuation methodology, the result is even more striking. With the film's India valuation estimated at ₹150 crore — roughly double what was attributed to 2021's Spider-Man: No Way Home — the run delivered a return of about ₹353 crore, or 235%, earning a "super duper hit" verdict by the site's parameters.

Tom Holland and Marvel's India Boom

The result is inseparable from Tom Holland's pull with Indian audiences. Spider-Man is arguably the most universally recognised Western superhero brand in India, built over three Holland-led films and reinforced by a young, English-comfortable urban audience that treats Marvel event films the way earlier generations treated Rajinikanth or Salman Khan releases — as opening-weekend rituals. The ensemble — Holland alongside Zendaya, Sadie Sink, Jacob Batalon, Jon Bernthal and Mark Ruffalo — gave the film crossover appeal across demographics.

For the diaspora, the takeaway is straightforward: the Indian box office is no longer a side market for Hollywood. With grosses approaching ₹600 crore for a single franchise instalment, India now ranks among the most consequential territories for global tentpoles — studios will court Indian audiences with localised marketing, dubbed versions, and release timing, the way they already do for China and Japan.

What's Next

The question now is whether Brand New Day's run is a franchise-specific peak or the new normal. Marvel's pipeline — including the upcoming Avengers instalments — will be the real test of whether ₹500-crore Hollywood runs are repeatable. For now, the film exits theatres with its place in Indian box office history secure: the second-biggest hit of 2026, and proof that in India, Spider-Man sells.
